steps.content: In your office, Nightingale is briefing you on the aftermath of the Wisteria Mania incident.

Due to widespread exposure to the dream, both the Drifter Camp and Eastside are showing elevated M-values and increased Mania fluctuations. Several Mania incidents have already occurred in Eastside's outskirts, resulting in casualties.

The situation at the Drifter Camp is deteriorating as well. The peripheral buildings, still under repair from previous damage, have been attacked again. The FAC has already dispatched forces and equipment, and the MBCC needs to send support as well.
You rub your tired eyes as you stare at the lengthy task list before you.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: There's still so much to be done... I should make time to visit the Drifter Camp, see what else we can do for them...
Knock, knock, knock...
The urgent knocking interrupts Nightingale's report, and before you can say come in, Wuhuanzi barges through the door.

steps.speaker: Wuhuanzi
steps.content: Ch... Chief! Would you spare a moment? It's something urgent.
Wuhuanzi is clutching a copy of the newspaper the Bureau subscribes to, her face flushed from what appears to be a rushed journey here.
She rarely comes here, except when it's to offer medical consultations or insist on treating your ailments.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Nightingale, proceed with the standard procedures for now. Email me about any tasks that need my attention.
Taking the hint, Nightingale picks up her device and leaves, leaving you two alone.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: We're alone now. Tell me what's on your mind.

steps.speaker: Wuhuanzi
steps.content: I need... a permit to leave, now.
Early the next morning, you drive from the Bureau to the Drifter Camp by the shortest route. Having visited countless times before, you know these streets like the back of your hand.
This time, however, you let Wuhuanzi take the lead. After all, you're only here as her official escort for this emergency leave.

steps.speaker: Wuhuanzi
steps.content: I'm sorry... If we hadn't been in such a hurry, you wouldn't have blown out that tire right after we left.

steps.speaker: Wuhuanzi
steps.content: I drew a divination stick last night. The reading warned of obstacles ahead, so this must be my misfortune at work again. I'll pay you back with the money I make from my consultations.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Stop blaming your misfortune for everything.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: I was just showing off my amazing driving skills. Thought I'd give the spare tire a chance to shine.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: This counts as an official expense. I can probably get reimbursed.

steps.speaker: Wuhuanzi
steps.content: Really? Would Adjutant Nightingale approve of that?

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: She will... probably.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: The funeral begins in less than thirty minutes. Your task now is to locate where it's being held, and fast.

steps.speaker: Wuhuanzi
steps.content: I need... a permit to leave, now.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: What's your reason?
Wuhuanzi rarely requests to go out except for purchasing herbs. This must be something important.

steps.speaker: Wuhuanzi
steps.content: A few months ago, I treated an old lady at the Drifter Camp.

steps.speaker: Wuhuanzi
steps.content: I know I cured her... So why is her name in the obituaries? Something must have gone wrong...
Wuhuanzi's fingernails are digging into the newspaper. You gently pry her fingers away and take the paper for a closer look.
The newspaper is crammed with reports of events from every corner of DisCity. Where her fingers left their marks is a tiny, perfectly square column tucked away in the corner of the page.

This section carries the names of the deceased without embellishment or flowery words. Some days the list runs long, others short. The obituary notes the funeral will be held tomorrow morning at the Drifter Camp.

steps.speaker: Wuhuanzi
steps.content: Did I miss something? Could there have been an underlying condition I failed to spot? Or was there something wrong with the medicine I prescribed...
Wuhuanzi paces anxiously before you, frantically going through every detail of her treatment, desperate to find some explanation for the elderly woman's death.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: I remember her name from the medical reports. You did cure her condition. There might be some misunderstanding in there. Her death may not have anything to do with your treatment. Try to stay calm.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: The Bureau receives multiple Mania incident reports every day. The Drifter Camp hasn't been peaceful lately...
As you watch Wuhuanzi's anxious demeanor, you recall something she said before.
Is Wuhuanzi so concerned about the elderly woman's death because she's worried about her good karma? Would the good karma she earns from healing someone vanish upon their death?

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: What are you hoping to find at the Drifter Camp?
Wuhuanzi lifts her head to meet your gaze. Her tone is earnest and slightly imploring.

steps.speaker: Wuhuanzi
steps.content: I need to verify the true cause of Granny Wu's death.

Contrary to your assumption, Wuhuanzi doesn't mention anything about good karma. Perhaps she isn't as obsessed with it as she claims to be. Right now, she's simply a doctor who's concerned about her patient's life.
You sense that a chance to understand Wuhuanzi's true thoughts is about to present itself.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Let's go.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: A Sinner needs a supervisor for emergency outings, right?

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: And... a driver.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: The permit is approved.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: The MBCC isn't some heartless organization, you know.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Think of it as... paying our last respects to that old lady.

steps.speaker: Wuhuanzi
steps.content: ...This is it. We're here.
By the time you arrive, the funeral is about to begin.

This appears to be where the old lady lived. Her modest home has been transformed into a simple memorial hall, too small to accommodate more than a few people inside. Neighbors who can't get in crowd around the doorway.
Wuhuanzi tries to squeeze through the crowd several times without success. She can only stand on tiptoes, eagerly peering inside over people's shoulders.

steps.speaker: Gossiping Neighbor A
steps.content: How did Ms. Wu pass away so suddenly? Didn't she recover from her leg condition? I heard she was even looking for part-time work.

steps.speaker: Gossiping Neighbor B
steps.content: Who knows? Maybe she wasn't really cured at all. I remember that doctor. She was muttering strange things constantly and looking so gloomy. Probably just another quack.

steps.speaker: Gossiping Neighbor C
steps.content: Don't spread rumors! I heard Ms. Wu encountered a Corruptor while working outside the Drifter Camp. That's what happened!

steps.speaker: Gossiping Neighbor A
steps.content: Sigh... What's the point of going through the treatment? She still ended up dead all the same.

steps.speaker: Gossiping Neighbor B
steps.content: I warned her not to wander around outside. Just look how dangerous it is out there these days. If she had just stayed home, none of this would have happened.

steps.speaker: Gossiping Neighbor D
steps.content: How can you talk like that? What's wrong with getting treatment? Try to show some respect!
The neighbors continue their back-and-forth, each chiming in with their own opinion.

steps.speaker: Wuhuanzi
steps.content: ...Is it all pointless? Do you also think that... in times like these, saving lives is just a futile effort?
Amid the bustling crowd and murmured condolences, Wuhuanzi stops in her tracks. She echoes fragments of their conversation softly as her hand withdraws timidly.
For a doctor... for Wuhuanzi, each life is one she's literally wrestled away from death's grasp. How could anyone dismiss such an achievement so casually?
You've witnessed Wuhuanzi's medical expertise firsthand. Calling her a quack based on groundless rumors is not only unfair to her, but also a disrespect to the lives she's saved.
You approach Wuhuanzi, words of comfort on the tip of your tongue, but as funeral music begins to play, she hurries away as if fleeing.
Natural light barely reaches the heart of the Drifter Camp, and lights stay on constantly as the only source of illumination. After Wuhuanzi leaves the funeral, you quietly follow her.
After walking for a while, Wuhuanzi gradually slows down until she's walking side by side with you.

steps.speaker: Wuhuanzi
steps.content: I've heard such talk many times before. It doesn't bother me anymore.
Wuhuanzi speaks with an air of detachment, as if she's used to numbing herself with these words.
The young wandering healer returns to the Drifter Camp to check on her former patient, only to be met with misunderstandings and wounded by cruel rumors.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Does it really not bother you, or have you just grown used to it?
Wuhuanzi comes to a stop beside you, your question giving her the courage to speak.

steps.speaker: Wuhuanzi
steps.content: If it were you... If you knew that saving someone now might expose them to greater dangers later, and you'd be misunderstood by others for it, would you still offer your help?
Seeing the dejection in Wuhuanzi's expression, you carefully choose your words, keeping your tone gentle.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Eastia and DisCity are worlds apart in everything. Language, mythology, theoretical frameworks, and even fundamental ways of thinking.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: You're a doctor, and I'm the Chief of the MBCC. We operate in completely different environments, with entirely different approaches to saving lives.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: I'm not confident I can give you a good answer simply by applying my imagination. And I know my answer won't be useful to you right away. But I can share with you my personal experience at the Drifter Camp. Would you like to hear my perspective?
Wuhuanzi nods, and you both head toward the bustling street. You've barely taken a few steps when someone recognizes you.

steps.speaker: Local A
steps.content: ...Oh? If it isn't ${PlayerName}!

steps.speaker: Local A
steps.content: It's been ages since you last visited! Check out my new home. Just finished rebuilding it yesterday. What do you think?

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: It looks very nice!

steps.speaker: Local B
steps.content: ${PlayerName}, you wouldn't believe it. A Corruptor broke in yesterday, but our guys from Rustfire managed to take care of it.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Mania incidents have been on the rise lately. Stay safe, and get those outer defenses rebuilt as soon as you can.
As you discuss Mania and reconstruction, Wuhuanzi timidly interjects with a question.

steps.speaker: Wuhuanzi
steps.content: Why rebuild it?

steps.speaker: Local B
steps.content: Hmm? What's that, young lady?

steps.speaker: Wuhuanzi
steps.content: I said... With so many Corruptors out there, why not move somewhere safer instead of rebuilding this place?

steps.speaker: Local B
steps.content: Huh? But this is our home. When something breaks in your home, you fix it up. Can't just abandon it now, can we...
Before you can form a response to Wuhuanzi's question, more locals recognize you and crowd around.

steps.speaker: Local C
steps.content: ${PlayerName}, I think I've developed a sleepwalking problem! In my dream, I was circling around this huge wisteria tree, and when I woke up, I found myself on top of the awning above the market!
Some shake your hand enthusiastically, others sob and sniffle as they pour out their troubles. There are even people asking you to sign some old photos of you, hoping to sell them for a good price...

steps.speaker: Option
options: Find a way to slip away

choices.text: Find a way to slip away

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Everyone, please calm down. I'm here today to assess the impact of the Mania incidents.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Please, don't crowd around.
After addressing everyone's concerns and questions, the crowd finally disperses.
Just as you think you finally have time to answer Wuhuanzi's question, another local approaches you hesitantly.

steps.speaker: Local D
steps.content: So you're the renowned...

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Yes, yes, that's me. Happy to be of service.

steps.speaker: Local D
steps.content: ${PlayerName}, you see, my old man's a little superstitious. He keeps forcing me to buy all sorts of protective charms to hang around the house. Ancient coins, peach wood swords, even crosses and garlic...

steps.speaker: Local D
steps.content: Sigh, I don't know how to reason with him. He keeps saying we must be cursed with bad luck, that's why we keep suffering through these disasters.

steps.speaker: Local D
steps.content: Then he starts going on about how I'm not trying hard enough. Says I need to defy destiny, or else don't bother coming home.
You give a simplified explanation for the Wisteria incident, sharing only the information cleared for public knowledge.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: This has nothing to do with luck or personal effort. Mania, Corruptors, and even Black Rings are real threats that exist whether we like it or not, crises that we all need to face together.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: As for those lucky charms... if they really worked, we wouldn't need the Public Security Bureau or FAC. We could all just pray our problems away.
The man leaves after giving his thanks, but not before insisting you take his newly bought lucky bracelet.
After watching you field question after question from everyone, Wuhuanzi fixes you with a serious look and poses one of her own.

steps.speaker: Wuhuanzi
steps.content: My friend, do you think... that a person's fortune has nothing to do with how hard they try?
You can't help but shake your head in amusement. Why is everyone coming to you with questions today? Do you really look like some kind of walking fortune cookie dispenser?

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: I believe... luck is nothing more than probability. I consider myself a hardworking person, but that doesn't seem to improve my luck one bit.
I even died once. You only add inwardly.

steps.speaker: Wuhuanzi
steps.content: What about lucky charms? Have you ever tried using them?

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: You mean this?
You show her the lucky bracelet the local just gave you. With a gentle tug, the string breaks, and before you can catch it, the beads are scattering all over.
With a patter, the beads bounce erratically before rolling to a stop next to Wuhuanzi's and your feet.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: If it can't even hold itself together, how's it supposed to protect me? See? Now I even have to try to put it back in one piece.
Wuhuanzi kneels down helpfully beside you, helping to pick up the scattered beads one by one.

steps.speaker: Wuhuanzi
steps.content: Then... if neither effort nor lucky charms work, what can I do to avoid disaster, to escape all this... misfortune?

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Shouldn't Eastian philosophy have explanations for this? I don't know much about it, but I remember you practice divination and consult almanacs.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: And what about your talismans, your peach wood sword, all these... tools you carry? Shouldn't you know better than me about these things?

steps.speaker: Option
options: Don't tell me you're not sure about them either?

choices.text: Don't tell me you're not sure about them either?

steps.content: Wuhuanzi rises to her feet, staring down at the collected beads in her hands, her long bangs hiding her eyes. Standing before you now, she somehow resembles a student seeking guidance from a teacher.
After a long while, she answers in a stifled voice.

steps.speaker: Wuhuanzi
steps.content: I'm indeed not sure...

steps.speaker: Wuhuanzi
steps.content: In the books I've studied, it is written that virtue brings fortune to those who practice it, and that morality is the foundation of all things.

steps.speaker: Wuhuanzi
steps.content: I kept telling myself that healing others was just to accumulate good karma, that everything would get better once I'd earned enough. But it seems... I never really convinced myself of that.
Now it's your turn to be confused.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Are you saying you've been lying to yourself? Why?
Wuhuanzi's brows knit together. Her lips part a few times and press shut again.

steps.speaker: Wuhuanzi
steps.content: Back in the interrogation room, when I said I was accumulating good karma to break my misfortune... I wasn't lying to you. I just... withheld certain things...

steps.speaker: Wuhuanzi
steps.content: My misfortune wasn't something I was born with. It came from the disaster that destroyed my hometown.
